newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says haze affects air links, shipping.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says haze affects air links, shipping.

text.p: A thick haze caused by forest fires has enveloped parts of Indonesia, disrupting air and sea transport, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.
Officials in neighbouring Malaysia issued health warnings, saying rising pollution there was also likely to have been caused by the fires.
Antara quoted officials as saying fires in various provinces on the islands of Java and Sumatra and in Kalimantan on the Indonesian portion of Borneo island were causing the hazy conditions.
They said the haze was likely to worsen as more dry weather was forecast for the next few months.

"It is predicted that the haze would become more serious in September and October in line with increases in temperature," the news agency quoted Meteorological and Geophysics Agency official Paulus Agus Winarso as saying.
"This condition generates drought, forest fires and creates a haze in the country."
Antara said Simpang Tiga airport on Sumatra and Tjilik Riwut airport in Central Kalimantan province were temporarily closed last week as visibility dropped due to the haze.
Pontianak airport in West Kalimantan was also affected, leading to long delays in flights landing there, it said.
Several flights were cancelled, Antara added.
Sea transport was also affected due to low visibility that persisted until late in the day, it said.

Skies around the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country have been hazy over the past couple of weeks, probably because of fires on Sumatra, which lies across the Malacca Strait, Malaysian officials said.
Government officials advised the public to refrain from outdoor exercise and schools have been told to limit outdoor activities.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, in remarks at the weekend, offered to help pay the costs of putting out the Indonesian forest fires.
In 1994, smoke from coal and forest fires raging in Sumatra and Kalimantan blew across Southeast Asia, shrouding Malaysia, Singapore and other parts of Indonesia for several months.
